forces.title: AI aggregates consumer attention, shifting ad visibility
forces.description: Consumer discovery is increasingly moving into AI-driven environments, with over 50% of Google searches including AI-generated overviews and up to 50% of open-web search traffic at risk by 2030. Within walled gardens like Instagram and TikTok, algorithmic feeds now drive most content consumption. This structural shift means brands' visibility increasingly depends on a few AI systems, impacting how ad tech connects advertisers to audiences and necessitating adaptation to AI-driven ranking and recommendation logic.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI agents mediate purchases, reshaping advertising's role
forces.description: AI is increasingly mediating consumer purchase decisions, with shopping agents and AI assistants ranking products, comparing alternatives, and even completing transactions on users' behalf. Early deployments show AI-enabled shopping experiences achieving up to 60% higher conversion rates. This fundamental shift means advertising success is less about securing data-driven impressions and more about being surfaced, recommended, and selected by these AI systems. Ad tech must evolve to enable brands to influence AI-native purchasing journeys, focusing on structured data and measurable outcomes.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI bundles capabilities, concentrating value in walled gardens
forces.description: As consumer attention, decision-making, buying, conversion, and measurement converge into integrated AI-driven environments, value is increasingly concentrating within AI-native platforms and walled gardens. These platforms bundle capabilities into single, AI-managed products, drawing value away from traditional intermediaries like ad exchanges, ad networks, and agencies that historically connected buyers and signals separately. This trend shifts the balance of power, increasing advertisers' dependence on platform-provided data and potentially reducing transparency for ad tech outside these integrated ecosystems.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Direct ad buying gains traction, bypassing programmatic intermediaries
forces.description: AI is reinforcing the growing trend of direct ad buying, which has nearly tripled between 2019 and early 2024. With discovery, buying, and measurement becoming more integrated within platforms, advertisers increasingly bypass traditional agencies and programmatic intermediaries. They prefer to work directly with walled gardens and AI-native platforms offering automated targeting, superior data, closed-loop measurement, and transaction visibility. This trend poses a significant challenge for ad tech companies built on intermediation and cross-platform arbitrage, forcing them to redefine their value proposition.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Ad tech intermediaries face existential threat from AI
forces.description: The ad tech "middle" is undergoing severe compression due to the emergence of AI-native buying agents. These agents can replicate cross-platform optimization within a single workflow, potentially rendering obsolete key use cases for supply-side platforms (SSPs), ad exchanges, traditional demand-side platforms (DSPs), and undifferentiated middleware. As AI automates crucial advertising functions, the need for multiple intermediation layers focused on arbitrage diminishes, pressuring profitability and business models for many incumbent ad tech players.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Ad tech can thrive via neutral, cross-platform infrastructure
forces.description: Despite value concentration in walled gardens, an opportunity exists for ad tech to serve as critical connective tissue across diverse AI platforms. Advertisers still require neutral, cross-platform identity and measurement solutions to compare performance and manage spend effectively across various closed ecosystems. Ad tech companies can differentiate by offering independent AI performance audits, validation services, and secure clean-room partnerships, positioning themselves as trusted, unbiased providers of essential advertising infrastructure.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Advertisers reallocate spend to AI-driven ad formats and platforms
forces.description: Advertisers are actively reallocating media spend, with over 50% investing in ads embedded in AI-generated answers and experimenting with AI-assisted commerce environments. Approximately 40% of this reallocated spend is shifting from traditional search and the open web towards platforms with superior data, measurement, and transaction capabilities. This indicates a growing preference for AI-integrated advertising solutions, presenting both a tailwind for innovative ad tech and a challenge for traditional ad inventory providers to adapt.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI erodes open web economics, pressuring publishers
forces.description: AI is accelerating the decline of traditional search traffic and the eroding economics of the open web, making click-driven, scale-dependent publishing increasingly unviable. Long-tail, SEO-dependent sites without user subscription models are particularly exposed. Publishers must seek alternative monetization beyond impression-based models, such as licensing content to AI platforms, building generative engine optimization (GEO) capabilities for AI answers, or pooling authenticated audiences into curated ecosystems. This shift impacts ad tech dependent on open web inventory and traditional measurement.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Increasing cyber risks and data protection concerns impact ad tech
forces.description: The Computers & Telecoms sector, which includes ad tech, faces ongoing geopolitical, energy, and supply-chain pressures, with cybersecurity remaining a key concern following major attacks in 2025. Cyber-security, data protection, and evolving regulatory frameworks are becoming defining themes for 2026. This elevates operational and compliance risks for ad tech companies, requiring significant investment in resilience and security measures to protect sensitive advertiser and user data and maintain trust in automated advertising systems.

forces.title: Retailers cut advertising amid weak consumer confidence
forces.description: The UK retail sector is under pressure from volatile consumer confidence, inflation, and higher interest rates constraining disposable income. Businesses are reducing spending, particularly in advertising and marketing, and adopting a "wait and see" stance on capital expenditure. This translates into reduced demand for advertising services, including digital advertising and ad tech solutions, as retailers prioritize cost-cutting and cash protection in a challenging economic environment, creating a cyclical headwind for the ad tech industry.

forces.title: Public favors social media ban for under-16s, risking audience reduction
forces.description: A significant portion of the UK public, including 75% of women and 52% of Gen Z, favors a social media ban for individuals under 16 years old, with 60% of all respondents agreeing. Such a ban, if implemented, would substantially reduce the addressable audience on social media platforms for advertisers, particularly those targeting younger demographics. This presents a key regulatory risk for the digital advertising ecosystem, including ad tech providers reliant on social media inventory and audience data.

forces.title: AI-generated scam content erodes trust in social media advertising
forces.description: Approximately one-in-six (15%) social media users who encountered AI-generated content believe its main purpose was to scam or defraud them. This perception of fraudulent AI content, impacting 10% of the total population, poses a significant risk to the credibility and trustworthiness of social media platforms and, by extension, the digital advertising ecosystem. It could lead to increased user skepticism, regulatory scrutiny, and a potential reduction in advertiser confidence or willingness to invest in social media advertising.

forces.title: Gaming offers significant, underpenetrated ad revenue opportunity
forces.description: Gaming represents a large, underpenetrated channel with high-quality, differentiated ad inventory, especially on PC and console where ad integration is nascent (4% of revenue). Mobile gaming advertising already accounts for ~50% of monetization, demonstrating scaled potential. Carefully designed in-game advertising can provide high-margin, incremental revenue, diversify income, and unlock brand marketing budgets. This offers a significant upside for ad tech to develop scalable, programmatic solutions that preserve player experience while monetizing valuable attention.
forces.source_title: Gaming’s next growth era: Unlocking the value of attention

viewpoints.title: AI to increase total media spend and ad return on investment
viewpoints.description: Three-quarters of advertisers surveyed expect AI to boost overall media spend in the next 12 months, driven by new use cases like AI shopping agents and improved return on ad spend (ROAS). One-third of advertisers anticipate over a 10 percent increase in ROAS due to AI integration. This indicates a positive outlook for the advertising ecosystem, including ad tech that leverages AI, as marketers reallocate budgets to optimize performance and explore new AI-driven engagement formats.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Ad tech intermediaries face compression from AI-native buying agents
viewpoints.description: The traditional ad tech "middle" is shrinking as AI-native buying agents emerge, capable of cross-platform optimization within single workflows. This development threatens to eliminate key functions of supply-side platforms (SSPs), ad exchanges, traditional demand-side platforms (DSPs), and undifferentiated middleware. As AI automates buying, optimization, and measurement, the intermediation layers built on cross-platform arbitrage will play a diminished role, necessitating strategic adaptation for survival in the evolving ecosystem.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Ad tech can thrive by owning neutral, cross-platform infrastructure
viewpoints.description: Ad tech companies can remain relevant and grow by acting as connective tissue across walled gardens and AI platforms. While closed ecosystems will develop internal infrastructure, advertisers still value neutral, cross-platform identity and measurement for comparing performance and managing spend. Offering independent AI performance audits, validation, and testing platforms, especially through clean-room partnerships, establishes a defensible position based on neutrality and trust, critical competitive differentiators in the AI-driven advertising economy.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

demand_drivers.description: Increasing investment by brands in commerce media networks as a channel to reach consumers closer to the point of purchase.
Growing allocation of marketing spend towards digital channels that demonstrate direct sales impact and closed-loop measurement.

pnl_drivers.description: Carefully designed advertising in platforms like gaming can provide significant incremental revenue, reducing dependence on other monetization methods and improving overall ARPU.

Mobile in-game advertising already represents ~50% of monetization.
